extracted.intended_audience: OSHA-covered employers, industry stakeholders, regulatory commenters, and analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and explains OSHA's proposed employer requirements for responding to heat-related illness/emergencies and the agency's cost-estimation methodology (labor vs capital costs, unit‑cost multiplications, frequency and discounting assumptions) as presented in the NPRM tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer response requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All covered employers would be required to respond when employees are experiencing signs and symptoms of heat-related illness or when there is a heat-related emergency at their work sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline regulatory duty discussed in this section; the subsequent cost estimates and tables quantify the costs of meeting that requirement (medical response, contacting EMS, transport, and supplies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of total costs for responding to heat-related illnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA calculates the total costs associated with responding to heat-related illnesses by multiplying the labor-based unit cost by the number of affected establishments and the number of heat-related illnesses per establishment (shown in table VIII.C.6.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the illness-response cost formula used in the economic analysis (labor-based only for non-emergency illness responses); table VIII.C.6. supplies the illness frequency inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of total costs for responding to heat-related emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA calculates the total costs associated with responding to heat-related emergencies as a sum of total labor-based costs and capital-based costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total labor-based costs are calculated by multiplying the labor-based unit costs by the number of affected establishments and the number of heat-related emergencies per establishment (also shown in table VIII.C.6.). Total capital-based costs are calculated by multiplying the capital-based unit costs by the number of affected establishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor-based unit cost components during emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Labor-based unit costs incurred during heat-related emergencies consist of reducing an employee's body temperature before emergency medical services arrive as well as contacting emergency medical services and transporting employees to a place where they can be reached by an emergency medical provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated activities define what OSHA counts as labor costs in emergency situations (on-site cooling actions, EMS contact, transport). They are the labor inputs used in the labor-based unit cost multiplications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital-based unit cost components
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital-based unit costs consist of ice, ice sheets, and ice coolers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are treated as capital or equipment inputs in the emergency-response costing. The analysis treats purchases of some of these items differently in frequency (see 'Cost frequency assumptions').

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost frequency assumptions for ice-related items
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost frequency is assumed to be one-time for purchases of ice sheets and ice coolers and the costs of purchasing ice when the initial heat trigger is met or exceeded are calculated on an annual basis. OSHA assumes that ice costs are incurred only when the initial heat trigger is met or exceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the temporal treatment of capital vs consumable costs: ice sheets and coolers are one-time capital purchases (annualized elsewhere), while ice (consumable) is an ongoing annual cost tied to the trigger condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ice cost calculation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Using this assumption, OSHA multiplied the number of 8-hour work shift equivalents by the number of affected establishments and the unit cost for ice to determine the total annual costs associated with ice purchases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the formula/inputs OSHA used to annualize consumable ice costs (shift equivalents × affected establishments × unit ice cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annualization and discounting of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Table VIII.C.26. shows the annualized one-time, annual, and total annualized costs for each of these requirements by industry category and region, discounted (2 percent over a 10-year period) and undiscounted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA presents both undiscounted (0%) and discounted (2% over 10 years) annualized presentations so readers can see both bases; the 2%/10-year discounting assumption is part of the costing methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost categories and table subheadings
rubrics_metrics.description: The analysis presents cost line-items under headings such as 'Medical Response—Non-Emergency', 'Medical Response—Emergency', 'Contact Emergency Medical Services', 'Transport Worker', 'Ice Sheets', 'Ice', and 'Ice Cooler' organized by industry category and region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category is tabulated by industry and region with columns for one-time annualized (0% and 2%), annual, and total annualized costs. These categories reflect the distinct types of costs OSHA attributes to compliance with response and planning requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry and regional breakdown requirement for cost reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA reports costs for each cost category by industry category (e.g., Construction, Manufacturing, Commercial Kitchens, etc.) and by region (Alaskan, Central, Eastern, Pacific, Southern, Western).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tables provide granular cost estimates per industry and region; this is part of the rulemaking economic disclosure and supports sectoral impact assessment and notice-and-comment review by affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding and presentation note
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to rounding, figures in the columns and rows may not sum to the totals shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological caveat about tabulated numerical presentation—useful for commenters checking arithmetic reconciliation or auditing inputs/outputs.
